failure_summary.description: Model consistently outputs overly descriptive or expanded answers (full names, added qualifiers, generic descriptions) instead of the exact concise term expected.
Skill lacks guidance for Jeopardy-style clues, causing the model to misinterpret statements as True/False questions or guess broadly rather than identifying the precise missing entity.

patch.reasoning: Every failure stems from the model failing to recognize Jeopardy-style trivia formats and producing verbose or descriptively altered answers. Adding explicit rules for handling statement-based clues, enforcing strict conciseness, and prioritizing exact entity extraction will align predictions with the expected short-form answers.

edits.content:
## Handling Jeopardy-Style Clues & Trivia Statements
- Questions may appear as incomplete sentences or factual statements rather than direct interrogatives. Treat these as fill-in-the-blank or identification queries.
- Answers must be strictly concise and match the exact expected term. Prefer last names over full names (e.g., "Genet" not "Jean Genet"), single letters/abbreviations if implied (e.g., "C" not "Vitamin C"), and bare entities without descriptive labels (e.g., "U2" not "U2 tribute band").
- Never interpret statement-based clues as True/False questions. Always identify the missing entity or term.
- When context contains multiple related terms, select the one that precisely completes the clue or matches the specific trivia fact, avoiding broad generalizations.
